source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה פְּסָל־לְךָ֛ שְׁנֵֽי־לֻחֹ֥ת אֲבָנִ֖ים כָּרִאשֹׁנִ֑ים וְכָתַבְתִּי֙ עַל־הַלֻּחֹ֔ת אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֛וּ עַל־הַלֻּחֹ֥ת הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שִׁבַּֽרְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first [ones], and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first [ones], and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Cut two new tablets out of stone, like the first pair. On them I will write the same words that stood on the first tablets, which you smashed.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Cut two more stone tablets like the first ones. I will write on them what was written on the first tablets, which you broke to pieces.

decisions.choice: which you broke: the first tablets, smashed at the foot of the mountain
decisions.reason: Moses broke the first tablets when he saw the golden calf (32:19). Those tablets were "the work of God" (32:16); now Moses must cut the stone himself, but God will again do the writing.

decisions.choice: I will write: God himself renews the broken covenant
decisions.reason: After Israel's sin with the calf, God does not hand the covenant over to be rewritten by a man. He promises to write the same words again (Deuteronomy 10:1-4). Compare verse 28, where the one who writes is less clear.

decisions.choice: smashed
decisions.reason: The verb means to break in pieces, as in 32:19. Balanced says "smashed"; Literal keeps "broke".

source.text: וֶהְיֵ֥ה נָכ֖וֹן לַבֹּ֑קֶר וְעָלִ֤יתָ בַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ אֶל־הַ֣ר סִינַ֔י וְנִצַּבְתָּ֥ לִ֛י שָׁ֖ם עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ הָהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And be prepared for the morning, and you will go up in the morning to [the] mountain of Sinai, and you will station yourself for me there on [the] top of the mountain.

en.L: And be ready for the morning, and go up in the morning to Mount Sinai, and station yourself there for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on the top of the mountain.
en.B: Be prepared for the morning. When it comes, climb Mount Sinai and take your place before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on its summit.
en.R: Be ready early tomorrow morning. Then climb Mount Sinai and meet {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} there at the top.

decisions.choice: station yourself: take a stand and wait, ready to meet God
decisions.reason: The verb means to take up a position and stand firm. God used it in 33:21 ("you shall stand on the rock"), where he promised to show Moses his glory. Here Moses is to wait for God to meet him.

decisions.choice: go up in the morning to Mount Sinai: a second ascent, like the first
decisions.reason: As in 19:20 and 24:12-18, Moses goes up the mountain to receive the tablets. This time he goes up alone (verse 3).

decisions.choice: meet me
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what taking a stand before God is for: meeting him.

source.text: וְאִישׁ֙ לֹֽא־יַעֲלֶ֣ה עִמָּ֔ךְ וְגַם־אִ֥ישׁ אַל־יֵרָ֖א בְּכָל־הָהָ֑ר גַּם־הַצֹּ֤אן וְהַבָּקָר֙ אַל־יִרְע֔וּ אֶל־מ֖וּל הָהָ֥ר הַהֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And anyone not he will go up with you, and also anyone not let him be seen on all the mountain; also the sheep and the cattle not let them graze to [the] front of the mountain, that [one].

en.L: And no one shall go up with you, and also let no one be seen on all the mountain; also the flocks and the herds, let them not graze in front of that mountain."
en.B: Nobody is to climb with you, and nobody else may be seen anywhere on the mountain. Keep even the flocks and herds from grazing near the front of that mountain."
en.R: No one may come up with you. No one may be anywhere on the mountain. Do not even let sheep or cattle eat grass near the mountain."

decisions.choice: let no one be seen on all the mountain: the mountain is holy ground
decisions.reason: When God came down on Sinai the first time, the people and their animals were kept back by a boundary (19:12-13, 21-24). The same holiness surrounds the mountain now. Not even Joshua, who went partway with Moses before (24:13), may come.

decisions.choice: the flocks and the herds: sheep and goats, and cattle
decisions.reason: The first word covers small livestock, both sheep and goats; the second means cattle. Together they mean all the animals.

source.text: וַיִּפְסֹ֡ל שְׁנֵֽי־לֻחֹ֨ת אֲבָנִ֜ים כָּרִאשֹׁנִ֗ים וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם מֹשֶׁ֤ה בַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ וַיַּ֨עַל֙ אֶל־הַ֣ר סִינַ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֹת֑וֹ וַיִּקַּ֣ח בְּיָד֔וֹ שְׁנֵ֖י לֻחֹ֥ת אֲבָנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he cut two tablets of stone like the first [ones], and rose early Moses in the morning and went up to [the] mountain of Sinai just as had commanded Yahweh him, and he took in his hand two tablets of stone.

en.L: And he cut two tablets of stone like the first [ones], and Moses rose early in the morning and went up to Mount Sinai, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him, and he took in his hand two tablets of stone.
en.B: So Moses cut two stone tablets like the first ones. Early next morning he went up Mount Sinai, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him, carrying the two stone tablets in his hand.
en.R: So Moses cut out two stone tablets like the first ones. He got up early the next morning and climbed Mount Sinai, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told him. He carried the two stone tablets with him.

decisions.choice: just as Yahweh had commanded him: Moses obeys exactly
decisions.reason: The phrase marks careful obedience to God's word (verses 1-2), as it does throughout the making of the tabernacle (39:1-43; 40:16).

decisions.choice: he cut ... Moses: the same person
decisions.reason: The first verb has no named subject; Moses is named in the next clause. He does what God told him in verse 1.

decisions.choice: So Moses cut
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Moses at the first verb and mark the obedience with "So".

source.text: וַיֵּ֤רֶד יְהוָה֙ בֶּֽעָנָ֔ן וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֥ב עִמּ֖וֹ שָׁ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְשֵׁ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And came down Yahweh in [the] cloud and stood with him there, and proclaimed (in) [the] name of Yahweh.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came down in the cloud and stood with him there, and proclaimed the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} came down in the cloud and took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place there beside Moses, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} announced {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} came down in a cloud and stood there with Moses. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} announced {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own name, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: proclaimed the name: Yahweh proclaims his own name
alternatives: Moses called on the name of Yahweh
decisions.reason: The subject of "stood" and "proclaimed" is not named again. In 33:19 God promised Moses, "I will proclaim the name 'Yahweh' before you", and in verse 6 Yahweh proclaims. So it is most likely God who announces his name here. The same words can mean "called on the name of Yahweh", as when Abram worshiped (Genesis 12:8; 13:4); then Moses would be the one calling.

decisions.choice: came down in the cloud: God's presence at Sinai
decisions.reason: God came down on Sinai in a thick cloud (19:9, 18-20) and spoke with Moses from the cloud at the tent of meeting (33:9-11). What God promised in 33:19-23 now happens.

decisions.choice: beside Moses / with Moses; his name
decisions.reason: "Him" is Moses, so Balanced and Readable name him. Because God himself proclaims the name (see the note), they say "his name".

source.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֨ר יְהוָ֥ה׀עַל־פָּנָיו֮ וַיִּקְרָא֒ יְהוָ֣ה׀יְהוָ֔ה אֵ֥ל רַח֖וּם וְחַנּ֑וּן אֶ֥רֶךְ אַפַּ֖יִם וְרַב־חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶֽת׀

records.literal_gloss: And passed by Yahweh before his face and proclaimed, Yahweh, Yahweh, God compassionate and gracious, long of anger(s) and great of steadfast love and faithfulness,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} passed by before his face and proclaimed, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a God compassionate and gracious, long of anger, and great in steadfast love and faithfulness,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} passed in front of Moses and called out, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a God of tender compassion and grace, slow to grow angry, rich in faithful love and in truth,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} passed in front of Moses and called out, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}! He is a God of tender mercy and kindness. He is slow to become angry. His faithful love is great, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} can always be trusted.

decisions.choice: proclaimed, "Yahweh, Yahweh": the name, spoken twice, begins the proclamation
alternatives: and Yahweh proclaimed: "Yahweh is a God compassionate ..."
decisions.reason: God passes by Moses, as promised in 33:22, and proclaims. The name may be called out twice for weight, or the first "Yahweh" may be the one who proclaims and the second the start of what is proclaimed ("Yahweh proclaimed: Yahweh is a God ..."). Either way, the words that follow describe who Yahweh is, the answer to Moses' prayer "show me your glory" (33:18-19).

decisions.choice: compassionate: tender, warm love that pities
decisions.reason: The word is related to the word for womb and describes the deep, protective love of a parent for a child (Psalm 103:13; Isaiah 49:15). In the Old Testament this adjective is used almost only of God.

decisions.choice: gracious: showing undeserved favor
decisions.reason: The word describes one who gives kindness that is not earned. Its root is the word for the "favor" Moses has found in God's eyes (33:12-17; 34:9).

decisions.choice: long of anger: slow to become angry, patient
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pictures anger as a nose or nostrils that are "long", slow to burn hot. It means patient and slow to punish (Proverbs 14:29; 16:32).

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyal, faithful love that keeps covenant
decisions.reason: The word means kindness and love that are loyal to a relationship and do not give up. It is the love God promised in 20:6 and showed in leading his people out of Egypt (15:13). "Great in" it means God has it in abundance.

decisions.choice: faithfulness: reliability, truth
decisions.reason: The word means firmness and reliability: being true, keeping one's word. Paired with steadfast love, it says that God's love can be depended on (Genesis 24:27; Psalm 25:10).

decisions.choice: the confession repeated through Scripture
decisions.reason: These words become Israel's confession of who God is. Moses quotes them when he pleads for the people (Numbers 14:18). They are echoed in Psalm 86:15, 103:8 and 145:8, Nehemiah 9:17, Joel 2:13 and Jonah 4:2. Joel and Jonah add that God "relents from disaster"; Jonah complains that God is like this toward Nineveh.

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "faithful love", as in 15:13 and 20:6; Literal says "steadfast love". Both carry the loyalty in the word, which "love" alone would lose.

decisions.choice: truth (Balanced); can always be trusted (Readable)
decisions.reason: With "faithful love" just before it, "faithfulness" would repeat the same idea in the same word. Balanced says "truth", in the sense of being true; Readable says what it means for God: he can be trusted. Literal keeps "faithfulness".

decisions.choice: long of anger
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase; Balanced says "slow to grow angry" and Readable "slow to become angry".

decisions.choice: He is ... He is ... His faithful love
decisions.reason: Readable turns the list of titles into short sentences about Yahweh, keeping the third person of the Hebrew.

source.text: נֹצֵ֥ר חֶ֨סֶד֙ לָאֲלָפִ֔ים נֹשֵׂ֥א עָוֺ֛ן וָפֶ֖שַׁע וְחַטָּאָ֑ה וְנַקֵּה֙ לֹ֣א יְנַקֶּ֔ה פֹּקֵ֣ד׀עֲוֺ֣ן אָב֗וֹת עַל־בָּנִים֙ וְעַל־בְּנֵ֣י בָנִ֔ים עַל־שִׁלֵּשִׁ֖ים וְעַל־רִבֵּעִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: keeping steadfast love to thousands, lifting iniquity and transgression and sin, and leaving unpunished not he leaves unpunished, visiting [the] iniquity of fathers on sons and on sons of sons, on third-generation and on fourth-generation.

en.L: keeping steadfast love to thousands, bearing iniquity and transgression and sin, but he will by no means acquit [the guilty], visiting the iniquity of fathers on {{gender:children|sons}} and on {{gender:children's children|sons' sons}}, on the third and on the fourth [generation]."
en.B: who keeps faithful love for thousands and forgives wrongdoing, rebellion and sin. Yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will never acquit the guilty; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings the wrongdoing of {{gender:parents|fathers}} upon their {{gender:children and grandchildren|sons and grandsons}}, to the third and the fourth generation."
en.R: He keeps showing faithful love to thousands. He forgives evil, rebellion and sin. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not let the guilty go free. He deals with the sin of {{gender:parents|fathers}} in the lives of their {{gender:children and grandchildren|sons and grandsons}}, even as far as the third and fourth generation."

decisions.choice: keeping steadfast love to thousands: love that lasts far beyond punishment
decisions.reason: "Keeping" means guarding and maintaining. "Thousands" stands against "the third and the fourth generation" at the end of the verse, so it may mean thousands of generations, as Deuteronomy 7:9 says ("to a thousand generations"; compare 20:6). It may also mean thousands of people. Either way God's love far outweighs his judgment.

decisions.choice: bearing iniquity and transgression and sin: forgiving sin of every kind
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift up and carry; with sin as its object it means to carry it away, to forgive (Psalm 32:1, 5). The three nouns are the main words for wrongdoing: iniquity (twisted, crooked wrong and the guilt it brings), transgression (rebellion, breaking faith) and sin (missing the mark). Together they mean every kind of wrong.

decisions.choice: he will by no means acquit: he will certainly not treat the guilty as innocent
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: "acquitting, he will not acquit". Its object, the guilty, is understood. Forgiveness does not mean that God pretends wrong was never done (Numbers 14:18; Nahum 1:3).

decisions.choice: visiting the iniquity of fathers on children: the effects of sin reach later generations
decisions.reason: To "visit" is to attend to, here to bring the consequences of wrongdoing. The third and fourth generations are the great-grandchildren and their children, the most that might live in one household together. In 20:5 the same words add "of those who hate me". Other passages make clear that each person answers for his own sin (Deuteronomy 24:16; Ezekiel 18:20).

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in verse 6; Literal says "steadfast love".

decisions.choice: will never acquit the guilty (Balanced); will not let the guilty go free (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name "the guilty" without brackets and render the doubled verb with "never" or a plain "not".

decisions.choice: deals with the sin of parents in the lives of
decisions.reason: Readable says what "visiting iniquity on" means in plain words: God's dealing with sin reaches the descendants. Literal keeps "visiting".

source.text: וַיְמַהֵ֖ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּקֹּ֥ד אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And hurried Moses and bowed low [to the] ground and bowed down.

en.L: And Moses hurried and bowed his head to the ground and bowed down.
en.B: Moses quickly sank down with his face to the ground in worship.
en.R: Right away Moses bowed down low to the ground and worshiped God.

decisions.choice: bowed low ... bowed down: knelt with his face to the ground and worshiped
decisions.reason: The first verb means to bow the head low; the second to bow down to the ground, the posture of worship (4:31; 12:27). Together they describe full reverence before God.

decisions.choice: hurried: at once
decisions.reason: "Hurried" goes with the following verbs: Moses bowed down without delay.

decisions.choice: worshiped God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one Moses worshiped.

source.text: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר אִם־נָא֩ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲדֹנָ֔י יֵֽלֶךְ־נָ֥א אֲדֹנָ֖י בְּקִרְבֵּ֑נוּ כִּ֤י עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹ֨רֶף֙ ה֔וּא וְסָלַחְתָּ֛ לַעֲוֺנֵ֥נוּ וּלְחַטָּאתֵ֖נוּ וּנְחַלְתָּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, if please I have found favor in your eyes, my Lord, let go please my Lord in our midst, for a people stiff of neck [is] it, and you will forgive our iniquity and our sin and you will take us as a possession.

en.L: And he said, "If, please, I have found favor in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes, my Lord, let my Lord, please, go in our midst, for it [is] a stiff-necked people; and pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance."
en.B: He said, "Lord, if I really have found favor with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, then please, Lord, go in our midst. These are a stubborn people. Forgive our wrongdoing and our sin, and claim us as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own possession."
en.R: Moses said, "Lord, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are pleased with me, please go along with us. These people are stubborn. But forgive our evil and our sin, and make us {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} very own people."

decisions.choice: if I have found favor in your eyes, my Lord: a respectful request
decisions.reason: The phrase is a polite way of asking a superior for something. God has already said that Moses has found favor in his eyes (33:12, 17). "My Lord" here is the title, not the divine name.

decisions.choice: for it is a stiff-necked people: the reason God must go with them
alternatives: although it is a stiff-necked people
decisions.reason: The small word can mean "for" or "although". God had said he would not go among them because they were stiff-necked, lest he destroy them (33:3, 5). Moses turns this around: because they are so stubborn, they need God among them, and his forgiveness. Read as "although", Moses admits their stubbornness and asks God to come anyway.

decisions.choice: take us as your inheritance: make us your own possession
decisions.reason: The verb means to take as an inheritance, a family's own land that is never sold. Moses asks God to claim Israel as his own for good (19:5; Deuteronomy 32:9).

decisions.choice: stubborn
decisions.reason: A stiff-necked animal will not turn when it is led (32:9; 33:3). Balanced and Readable say "stubborn"; Literal keeps "stiff-necked". Both leave open whether the clause gives a reason or a concession.

decisions.choice: if you are pleased with me
decisions.reason: Readable says what having found favor in God's eyes means.

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִי֮ כֹּרֵ֣ת בְּרִית֒ נֶ֤גֶד כָּֽל־עַמְּךָ֙ אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה נִפְלָאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־נִבְרְא֥וּ בְכָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ וּבְכָל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וְרָאָ֣ה כָל־הָ֠עָם אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֨ה בְקִרְבּ֜וֹ אֶת־מַעֲשֵׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי־נוֹרָ֣א ה֔וּא אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י עֹשֶׂ֥ה עִמָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, here! I [am] about to make a covenant. Before all your people I will do wonders which not they have been created in all the earth and among all the nations, and will see all the people which you [are] in its midst the work of Yahweh, that awesome [is] it, which I [am] about to do with you.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Look, I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will do wonders that have not been created in all the earth or in any of the nations, and all the people in whose midst you [are] shall see the work of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for it [is] awesome, what I am doing with you.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Here and now I am making a covenant. In front of all your people I will work marvels such as have never been brought into being anywhere on earth or in any nation. All the people among whom you live will see what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does, for what I am about to do with you will fill them with awe.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Listen! I am making a covenant with you. I will do amazing things in front of all your people. Nothing like them has ever been done anywhere in the world, in any nation. All the people around you will see what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} can do. What I am going to do with you will fill people with awe.

decisions.choice: created: brought into being by God alone
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in Genesis 1:1, and only God is ever its subject. The wonders will be new acts of God, without precedent (compare Numbers 16:30).

decisions.choice: all the people in whose midst you are: Israel, or the nations around
alternatives: the nations among whom you live
decisions.reason: "You" here is Moses, so "the people in whose midst you are" is most likely Israel itself, among whom Moses lives. It may also mean the peoples around Israel, who will see what God does for them (verse 11).

decisions.choice: awesome: inspiring fear and reverence
decisions.reason: The word describes what fills people with dread and wonder, as God's acts at the sea did (15:11).

decisions.choice: The LORD said
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he said"; Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

decisions.choice: a covenant with you
decisions.reason: Readable adds "with you" from verse 27, where God says he has made a covenant with Moses and with Israel.

source.text: שְׁמָ֨ר־לְךָ֔ אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י מְצַוְּךָ֣ הַיּ֑וֹם הִנְנִ֧י גֹרֵ֣שׁ מִפָּנֶ֗יךָ אֶת־הָאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י וְהַחִתִּי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י וְהַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Keep for yourself that which I [am] commanding you this day. Here I [am] about to drive out from before you the Amorite[s] and the Canaanite[s] and the Hittite[s] and the Perizzite[s] and the Hivite[s] and the Jebusite[s].

en.L: Keep for yourself what I am commanding you today. Look, I am driving out before you the Amorite and the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite.
en.B: Take care to keep what I am commanding you today. Watch: I am about to drive out ahead of you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.
en.R: Do what I am telling you today. I am going to force out the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites ahead of you.

decisions.choice: keep for yourself: take care to obey
decisions.reason: "Keep" means to watch over, and "for yourself" makes it personal: be careful to do it.

decisions.choice: the six peoples of the land
decisions.reason: The same peoples are listed in 3:8, 17, 23:23 and 33:2. They lived in Canaan before Israel.

decisions.choice: Amorites, Canaanites ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses singular names for each whole people. Balanced and Readable use plurals; Literal keeps the singular.

source.text: הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֗ פֶּן־תִּכְרֹ֤ת בְּרִית֙ לְיוֹשֵׁ֣ב הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֖ה בָּ֣א עָלֶ֑יהָ פֶּן־יִהְיֶ֥ה לְמוֹקֵ֖שׁ בְּקִרְבֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Take heed to yourself lest you make a covenant with [the] inhabitant[s] of the land which you [are] going to it, lest he become a snare in your midst.

en.L: Take heed to yourself lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land which you are going into, lest it become a snare in your midst.
en.B: Watch yourself, so that you make no covenant with the people living in the land you are entering; otherwise it will become a trap set in your midst.
en.R: Be careful not to make any agreement with the people who live in the land you are going into. If you do, it will be like a trap that catches you.

decisions.choice: snare: a trap that lures and catches
decisions.reason: A snare is a bird trap. A covenant with the peoples of the land would draw Israel into worshiping their gods (23:33; Judges 2:3).

decisions.choice: lest it become: the covenant, or the people
decisions.reason: The verb is singular. It may refer to the covenant, or to the inhabitants of the land taken together as one; in 23:33 it is their gods that would be a snare. The sense is the same: the tie would trap Israel.

decisions.choice: agreement
decisions.reason: The same word as God's covenant in verse 10. Here it is a treaty between peoples, so Readable says "agreement"; Literal and Balanced keep "covenant" to show the contrast with God's covenant.

source.text: כִּ֤י אֶת־מִזְבְּחֹתָם֙ תִּתֹּצ֔וּן וְאֶת־מַצֵּבֹתָ֖ם תְּשַׁבֵּר֑וּן וְאֶת־אֲשֵׁרָ֖יו תִּכְרֹתֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: But their altars you will pull down, and their sacred pillars you will break down, and its Asherah poles you will cut down.

en.L: But their altars you shall tear down, and their pillars you shall break, and their Asherah poles you shall cut down.
en.B: Rather, you are to tear down their altars, shatter their standing stones, and chop down their Asherah poles.
en.R: Instead, tear down their altars. Break their stone pillars used in worship. Cut down the wooden poles they use to worship the goddess Asherah.

decisions.choice: pillars: standing stones set up in worship
decisions.reason: These were upright stones set up at places of worship. Such stones could mark a place where God had met someone (Genesis 28:18; Exodus 24:4), but those of the Canaanites belonged to their gods and were to be destroyed (23:24; Deuteronomy 12:3).

decisions.choice: Asherah poles: wooden objects for the goddess Asherah
decisions.reason: Asherah was a Canaanite goddess. Her symbol was a wooden pole or a tree set up beside an altar, which could be cut down and burned (Judges 6:25-26; 2 Kings 23:6). The word names both the goddess and the object; its exact form is not known. This is its first appearance in the Bible.

decisions.choice: but: instead of making a covenant
decisions.reason: The opening word sets this against verse 12: rather than making a covenant with these peoples, Israel is to destroy their places of worship. "Its" Asherah poles refers to the people of the land taken as one.

decisions.choice: standing stones (Balanced); stone pillars used in worship (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the pillars were. Literal keeps "pillars".

decisions.choice: wooden poles they use to worship the goddess Asherah
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name, which a reader may not know.

source.text: כִּ֛י לֹ֥א תִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖ה לְאֵ֣ל אַחֵ֑ר כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ קַנָּ֣א שְׁמ֔וֹ אֵ֥ל קַנָּ֖א הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: For not you must bow down to a god another, for Yahweh, Jealous [is] his name, a God jealous [is] he.

en.L: For you shall not bow down to another god, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Jealous [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name; a jealous God [is] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}.
en.B: Bow down to no other god. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is named Jealous; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is a jealous God.
en.R: Do not worship any other god. The name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is Jealous. He is a jealous God who wants {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people to belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} alone.

decisions.choice: jealous: zealous for an undivided relationship
decisions.reason: The word describes the passion of one who will not share a loved one with a rival, as a husband will not share his wife. It is used only of God. He will not share his people's worship with other gods (20:5; Deuteronomy 4:24; 5:9).

decisions.choice: Jealous is his name: this is what he is
decisions.reason: A name in the Bible shows what someone is like. To say his name is Jealous means jealousy for his people belongs to who he is.

decisions.choice: who wants his people to belong to him alone
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "jealous" means here, since the word in common use often suggests envy.

source.text: פֶּן־תִּכְרֹ֥ת בְּרִ֖ית לְיוֹשֵׁ֣ב הָאָ֑רֶץ וְזָנ֣וּ׀אַחֲרֵ֣י אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֗ם וְזָבְחוּ֙ לֵאלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם וְקָרָ֣א לְךָ֔ וְאָכַלְתָּ֖ מִזִּבְחֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: lest you make a covenant with [the] inhabitant[s] of the land, and they will prostitute themselves after their gods and they will sacrifice to their gods, and [someone] will invite you, and you will eat of his sacrifice,

en.L: lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and they prostitute themselves after their gods and sacrifice to their gods, and [someone] invites you, and you eat of his sacrifice,
en.B: Do not make a covenant with the people who live in the land. For when they give themselves like prostitutes to their gods and offer sacrifices to them, someone will invite you, and you will eat from the sacrifice,
en.R: Do not make an agreement with the people who live in the land. When they worship their gods and offer sacrifices to them, they will invite you, and you will eat meat from their sacrifices.

decisions.choice: prostitute themselves after their gods: worship false gods, a picture of unfaithfulness
decisions.reason: The verb means to act as a prostitute. The Bible often uses it of worshiping other gods, because the covenant between God and his people is like a marriage, and turning to other gods is like adultery (Leviticus 20:5-6; Judges 2:17; Hosea 1-3).

decisions.choice: invite you and you eat of his sacrifice: sharing in their worship
decisions.reason: Part of many sacrifices was eaten by the worshipers in a meal. To eat such a meal was to share in the worship of the god it was offered to (Numbers 25:1-2; 1 Corinthians 10:20-21).

decisions.choice: worship their gods
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the picture without it. Literal says "prostitute themselves after"; Balanced "give themselves like prostitutes to".

decisions.choice: agreement
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

source.text: וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ מִבְּנֹתָ֖יו לְבָנֶ֑יךָ וְזָנ֣וּ בְנֹתָ֗יו אַחֲרֵי֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ן וְהִזְנוּ֙ אֶת־בָּנֶ֔יךָ אַחֲרֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: and you will take of his daughters for your sons, and will prostitute themselves his daughters after their gods, and they will make prostitute [themselves] your sons after their gods.

en.L: and you take of his daughters for your sons, and his daughters prostitute themselves after their gods and make your sons prostitute themselves after their gods.
en.B: and you will take some of their daughters as wives for your sons, and their daughters, prostituting themselves after their gods, will draw your sons after their gods in the same way.
en.R: Then you will choose some of their daughters as wives for your sons. Those daughters will worship their own gods, and they will lead your sons to turn away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and worship those gods too.

decisions.choice: take of his daughters for your sons: marriage with the peoples of the land
decisions.reason: Fathers arranged their sons' marriages. Marriage would join Israel's families to those who worshiped other gods (Deuteronomy 7:3-4). Solomon's foreign wives turned his heart to their gods (1 Kings 11:1-8).

decisions.choice: make your sons prostitute themselves: lead them into the same unfaithfulness
decisions.reason: The second verb is the causing form of the first: the daughters will cause Israel's sons to be unfaithful to God as they are.

decisions.choice: turn away from me and worship those gods
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the picture of prostitution means: leaving God for other gods.

source.text: אֱלֹהֵ֥י מַסֵּכָ֖ה לֹ֥א תַעֲשֶׂה־לָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Gods of molten metal not you must make for yourself.

en.L: Gods of cast metal you shall not make for yourself.
en.B: Do not make yourself gods cast from metal.
en.R: Do not make any metal statues of gods.

decisions.choice: gods of cast metal: like the golden calf
decisions.reason: The word is the one used of the calf Aaron made, a "calf of cast metal" (32:4, 8). The command repeats 20:4 and 20:23 in the light of that sin.

decisions.choice: metal statues of gods
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gods were: images made by pouring melted metal into a mold.

source.text: אֶת־חַ֣ג הַמַּצּוֹת֮ תִּשְׁמֹר֒ שִׁבְעַ֨ת יָמִ֜ים תֹּאכַ֤ל מַצּוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ךָ לְמוֹעֵ֖ד חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָאָבִ֑יב כִּ֚י בְּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽאָבִ֔יב יָצָ֖אתָ מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: The festival of the unleavened bread(s) you will keep; seven days you will eat unleavened bread(s), which I commanded you, at the appointed time [of] the month of the Abib, for in the month of the Abib you came out from Egypt.

en.L: The feast of unleavened bread you shall keep. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time of the month of Abib, for in the month of Abib you came out from Egypt.
en.B: Keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread: for seven days your bread is to be unleavened, as I commanded you, at its set time in the month of Abib, because it was in Abib that you left Egypt.
en.R: Keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread. Eat only unleavened bread, made without yeast, for seven days, just as I told you. Do this at the right time in the month of Abib, because that is the month when you left Egypt.

decisions.choice: Abib: the month of fresh ears of grain
decisions.reason: The name means fresh, ripening ears of barley. It is the first month of the year (12:2; 13:4; 23:15), about March to April.

decisions.choice: as I commanded you: the feast already given
decisions.reason: The Feast of Unleavened Bread was commanded in 12:15-20 and 13:3-10 and again in 23:15. Verses 18-26 repeat the commands of 23:12-19.

decisions.choice: Feast (Balanced); Festival (Readable)
decisions.reason: The festival names are capitalized at Balanced and Readable, as in 12:17. Readable adds "made without yeast".

source.text: כָּל־פֶּ֥טֶר רֶ֖חֶם לִ֑י וְכָֽל־מִקְנְךָ֙ תִּזָּכָ֔ר פֶּ֖טֶר שׁ֥וֹר וָשֶֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: Every opener of a womb [is] to me, and all your livestock [that] is male, [the] firstborn of ox and sheep.

en.L: Every opener of [the] womb [is] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}, and all your livestock [that is] male, the firstborn of ox and sheep.
en.B: Whatever first opens the womb is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}, including every male firstborn among your livestock, of cattle or of sheep and goats.
en.R: Every firstborn male belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. That includes the first male calf, lamb or young goat born to each of your animals.

decisions.choice: every opener of a womb: every firstborn
decisions.reason: The firstborn is the one who first opens its mother's womb. Firstborn males of people and animals belong to God because he spared Israel's firstborn in Egypt (13:2, 12-15).

decisions.choice: that is male: the firstborn males of the livestock
alternatives: all your livestock will be remembered
decisions.reason: The verb form here is unusual; as written it looks like "will be remembered". In this context, and as in 13:12 ("the males belong to Yahweh"), it is best read as "that is male". The Greek translation has "the males".

decisions.choice: sheep: one animal of the flock, a sheep or a goat
decisions.reason: The word means a single animal from the flock, either a sheep or a goat.

source.text: וּפֶ֤טֶר חֲמוֹר֙ תִּפְדֶּ֣ה בְשֶׂ֔ה וְאִם־לֹ֥א תִפְדֶּ֖ה וַעֲרַפְתּ֑וֹ כֹּ֣ל בְּכ֤וֹר בָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ תִּפְדֶּ֔ה וְלֹֽא־יֵרָא֥וּ פָנַ֖י רֵיקָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] firstborn of a donkey you will redeem with a sheep, and if not you will redeem [it], you will break its neck. Every firstborn of your sons you will redeem. And not they will be seen [before] my face empty.

en.L: And the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb, and if you do not redeem [it], you shall break its neck. Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem. And they shall not appear before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face empty.
en.B: Every firstborn donkey you are to redeem by giving a lamb in its place; if you will not redeem it, you must break its neck. And you are to redeem every firstborn son of yours. No one is to come before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with empty hands.
en.R: You must buy back each firstborn donkey by giving a lamb in its place. If you do not buy it back, you must break its neck. You must also buy back each of your firstborn sons. No one may come to worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} without bringing a gift.

decisions.choice: redeem: buy back by giving another in its place
decisions.reason: These laws repeat 13:13. A donkey could not be sacrificed, so a lamb was given in its place; a firstborn son was bought back, never sacrificed.

decisions.choice: not appear before my face empty: bring an offering when coming to worship
decisions.reason: To appear before God's face is to come to his sanctuary at the feasts. No one is to come without a gift from what God has given (23:15; Deuteronomy 16:16-17). The same words are in 23:15.

decisions.choice: redeem ... buy back
decisions.reason: As in 13:13: "redeem" at Literal and Balanced, "buy back" at Readable.

decisions.choice: without bringing a gift
decisions.reason: Readable says what "empty" means: without an offering.

source.text: שֵׁ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ תַּעֲבֹ֔ד וּבַיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י תִּשְׁבֹּ֑ת בֶּחָרִ֥ישׁ וּבַקָּצִ֖יר תִּשְׁבֹּֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: Six days you will labor and on the seventh day you will rest; in the plowing time and in the harvest time you will rest.

en.L: Six days you shall work, and on the seventh day you shall rest; in plowing [time] and in harvest you shall rest.
en.B: For six days you may do your work, but the seventh day you are to keep as a day of rest. Rest even when the fields need plowing or the harvest is ready.
en.R: You may work for six days, but on the seventh day you must rest. Rest on that day even in the busy times when you plow your fields and gather your crops.

decisions.choice: rest: stop work
decisions.reason: The verb means to cease, to stop working. The word Sabbath comes from it (16:30; 20:8-11; 23:12; 31:13-17).

decisions.choice: in plowing time and in harvest: even in the busiest seasons
decisions.reason: Plowing before the rains and harvest were the times farmers could least afford to stop. The Sabbath rest applies even then.

source.text: וְחַ֤ג שָׁבֻעֹת֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה לְךָ֔ בִּכּוּרֵ֖י קְצִ֣יר חִטִּ֑ים וְחַג֙ הָֽאָסִ֔יף תְּקוּפַ֖ת הַשָּׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And a festival of weeks you will observe for yourself, [the] first-fruits of [the] harvest of wheat, and the festival of the ingathering [at] the circuit of the year.

en.L: And a feast of weeks you shall keep for yourself, [with the] firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the feast of ingathering [at] the turn of the year.
en.B: Keep the Feast of Weeks when the first of the wheat harvest comes in, and the Feast of Ingathering as the year comes round.
en.R: Celebrate the Festival of Weeks when you bring in the first of your wheat harvest. Celebrate the Festival of Ingathering at the end of the farming year, when you gather in your crops.

decisions.choice: the Feast of Weeks: the start of the wheat harvest
decisions.reason: The feast came seven weeks after the start of the grain harvest (Leviticus 23:15-16; Deuteronomy 16:9-10), in late spring. Later it was called Pentecost, the "fiftieth" day (Acts 2:1).

decisions.choice: the Feast of Ingathering at the turn of the year: the autumn harvest
decisions.reason: This feast came when the last crops, grapes, olives and other fruits, were gathered in, as the farming year came round to its end (23:16 says "at the going out of the year"). It is also called the Feast of Booths (Leviticus 23:34-43).

decisions.choice: at the end of the farming year, when you gather in your crops
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the turn of the year" and the name "Ingathering".

source.text: שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים בַּשָּׁנָ֑ה יֵרָאֶה֙ כָּל־זְכ֣וּרְךָ֔ אֶת־פְּנֵ֛י הָֽאָדֹ֥ן׀יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Three times in the year he will present himself every male of yours before the face of the Lord Yahweh, the God of Israel.

en.L: Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the face of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.
en.B: Three times a year every male among you is to appear before the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.
en.R: Three times each year every male among you must come to worship the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: three times in the year all your males: the three pilgrim feasts
decisions.reason: The three times are the feasts of verses 18 and 22 (23:14-17; Deuteronomy 16:16). The men went as heads of their households; women and children might also go (1 Samuel 1:3-7).

decisions.choice: the Lord Yahweh: the Master, Yahweh
decisions.reason: "The Lord" is a title meaning master, set before the divine name. Together they stress that Yahweh is Israel's sovereign, whose servants must come before him.

decisions.choice: the Lord GOD
decisions.reason: When the title "Lord" stands just before the divine name, the name is printed "GOD" to avoid "the Lord LORD"; the Yahweh setting gives "the Lord Yahweh".

source.text: כִּֽי־אוֹרִ֤ישׁ גּוֹיִם֙ מִפָּנֶ֔יךָ וְהִרְחַבְתִּ֖י אֶת־גְּבוּלֶ֑ךָ וְלֹא־יַחְמֹ֥ד אִישׁ֙ אֶֽת־אַרְצְךָ֔ בַּעֲלֹֽתְךָ֗ לֵרָאוֹת֙ אֶת־פְּנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים בַּשָּׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For I will dispossess nations from before you and I will enlarge your territory, and not will covet anyone your land when you go up to present yourself before the face of Yahweh your God three times in the year.

en.L: For I will dispossess nations before you and enlarge your territory, and no one shall covet your land when you go up to appear before the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God three times in the year.
en.B: I will dispossess nations to make room for you and push your borders outward. And while you are away three times a year, going up to appear before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, no one will scheme to seize your land.
en.R: I will force nations out ahead of you and give you more land. Three times a year you will go to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. While you are gone, no one will try to take your land.

decisions.choice: no one shall covet your land when you go up: God guards what is left behind
decisions.reason: Going to the feasts meant leaving farms and towns unguarded. God promises that no one will even desire to take the land while his people worship him.

decisions.choice: covet: desire with intent to take
decisions.reason: The verb is the one in the command "you shall not covet" (20:17). It means desire that leads to taking.

decisions.choice: scheme to seize
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the intent in "covet"; Readable says "try to take".

source.text: לֹֽא־תִשְׁחַ֥ט עַל־חָמֵ֖ץ דַּם־זִבְחִ֑י וְלֹא־יָלִ֣ין לַבֹּ֔קֶר זֶ֖בַח חַ֥ג הַפָּֽסַח׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you must slaughter with leaven the blood of my sacrifice, and not will remain overnight to the morning [the] sacrifice of the festival of the Passover.

en.L: You shall not slaughter with leaven the blood of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sacrifice, and the sacrifice of the feast of the Passover shall not remain overnight until the morning.
en.B: When you slaughter a sacrifice for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, nothing leavened is to be offered with its blood. And nothing of the sacrifice of the Passover feast may be left over until morning.
en.R: When you offer an animal to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, do not offer any bread made with yeast at the same time. Do not keep any meat from the Passover sacrifice until the next morning.

decisions.choice: with leaven: leavened bread may not go with a sacrifice
decisions.reason: Leaven was kept from the altar (Leviticus 2:11). At Passover, above all, no leaven was to be present (12:15-20).

decisions.choice: not remain overnight until morning: the Passover meal is eaten that night
decisions.reason: As in 12:10, nothing of the Passover lamb was to be left until morning. Verse 25 repeats 23:18, here naming the Passover.

decisions.choice: leavened (Balanced); bread made with yeast (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in chapter 12: "leaven" at Literal and Balanced, "yeast" at Readable.

source.text: רֵאשִׁ֗ית בִּכּוּרֵי֙ אַדְמָ֣תְךָ֔ תָּבִ֕יא בֵּ֖ית יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹא־תְבַשֵּׁ֥ל גְּדִ֖י בַּחֲלֵ֥ב אִמּֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: The first of the first-fruits of your ground you will bring [to] the house of Yahweh your God. Not you will boil a kid in the milk of its mother.

en.L: The first of the firstfruits of your ground you shall bring [to] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk."
en.B: The choicest of the first produce from your land you are to bring into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Never boil a young goat in the milk of its own mother."
en.R: Bring the first and best crops from your fields to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Do not cook a young goat in the milk that came from its mother."

decisions.choice: the first: the first and the best
decisions.reason: The word means the beginning of something and also its best part. The earliest and finest of the harvest belongs to God (23:19; Numbers 18:12-13).

decisions.choice: not boil a young goat in its mother's milk: the reason is not given
decisions.reason: The command appears three times (23:19; 34:26; Deuteronomy 14:21). The text does not say why. It may forbid a practice of other peoples' worship, or protect the bond between mother and young, as other laws do (Leviticus 22:28; Deuteronomy 22:6-7).

decisions.choice: the house of Yahweh: God's sanctuary
decisions.reason: The house of Yahweh is the place where he dwells among his people: at first the tabernacle (25:8-9), later the temple.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כְּתָב־לְךָ֖ אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֞י עַל־פִּ֣י׀הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה כָּרַ֧תִּי אִתְּךָ֛ בְּרִ֖ית וְאֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, write for yourself these words, for on the mouth of these words I have made with you a covenant and with Israel.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Write for yourself these words, for according to the mouth of these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses, "Put these words in writing, for they are the terms on which I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses, "Write down these words. They are the terms of the covenant I have made with you and with Israel."

decisions.choice: on the mouth of these words: in accordance with these words
decisions.reason: "According to the mouth of" means "on the terms of". The words of verses 10-26 set out what the renewed covenant requires.

decisions.choice: write these words: the covenant is put in writing
decisions.reason: When the covenant was first made, Moses wrote down God's words and read them to the people (24:4, 7). He is now to write the words of the renewed covenant.

decisions.choice: the terms
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom. Literal keeps "according to the mouth of".

source.text: וַֽיְהִי־שָׁ֣ם עִם־יְהוָ֗ה אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יוֹם֙ וְאַרְבָּעִ֣ים לַ֔יְלָה לֶ֚חֶם לֹ֣א אָכַ֔ל וּמַ֖יִם לֹ֣א שָׁתָ֑ה וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב עַל־הַלֻּחֹ֗ת אֵ֚ת דִּבְרֵ֣י הַבְּרִ֔ית עֲשֶׂ֖רֶת הַדְּבָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he was there with Yahweh forty day[s] and forty night[s]; food not he ate and water not he drank. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten words.

en.L: And he was there with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} forty days and forty nights; bread he did not eat and water he did not drink. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten words.
en.B: Moses remained there with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for forty days and forty nights; he ate no food and drank no water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Words.
en.R: Moses stayed there with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for forty days and forty nights. During that time he did not eat any food or drink any water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments.

decisions.choice: he wrote: God, or Moses
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. In verse 1 God said, "I will write on the tablets", and Deuteronomy 10:2-4 says that God wrote the Ten Words on the second tablets. But Moses is the subject of the verbs just before, and in verse 27 God told him to write. The words Moses wrote may be those of verses 10-26, and the Ten Words those written by God.

decisions.choice: the ten words: the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: This is the Hebrew name for the commands of 20:1-17 (Deuteronomy 4:13; 10:4). "Words" here means sayings or commands.

decisions.choice: forty days and forty nights without food or water: as on the first ascent
decisions.reason: Moses spent forty days and nights on the mountain before (24:18), and he fasted again when he interceded for Israel (Deuteronomy 9:9, 18). Elijah traveled forty days to the same mountain (1 Kings 19:8), and Jesus fasted forty days in the wilderness (Matthew 4:2).

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he was there"; Balanced and Readable name Moses. They leave "he wrote" unnamed, as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: Readable uses the familiar name. Literal and Balanced keep "ten words", the Hebrew name.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י בְּרֶ֤דֶת מֹשֶׁה֙ מֵהַ֣ר סִינַ֔י וּשְׁנֵ֨י לֻחֹ֤ת הָֽעֵדֻת֙ בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁ֔ה בְּרִדְתּ֖וֹ מִן־הָהָ֑ר וּמֹשֶׁ֣ה לֹֽא־יָדַ֗ע כִּ֥י קָרַ֛ן ע֥וֹר פָּנָ֖יו בְּדַבְּר֥וֹ אִתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when Moses came down from [the] mountain of Sinai, and the two tablets of the testimony [were] in [the] hand of Moses when he came down from the mountain, and Moses not he knew that it shone [the] skin of his face because he had spoken with him.

en.L: And it happened, when Moses came down from Mount Sinai, and the two tablets of the testimony [were] in the hand of Moses when he came down from the mountain, that Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had spoken with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Moses came down from Mount Sinai holding the two tablets of the testimony. As he descended the mountain, he was unaware that the skin of his face shone with rays of light, because he had been speaking with God.
en.R: Moses came down from Mount Sinai carrying the two stone tablets of the covenant. As he came down the mountain, he did not know that his face was shining, because he had been talking with God.

decisions.choice: shone: sent out rays
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the noun for "horn" and is found only in this passage. It describes rays of light, like horns of light, shining from Moses' face (compare Habakkuk 3:4, where "rays" is the same noun). The Latin Vulgate read it as "horned", and that is why medieval and Renaissance art, including Michelangelo's statue of Moses, shows him with horns.

decisions.choice: the tablets of the testimony: the tablets of the covenant
decisions.reason: "The testimony" is the covenant written on the tablets, which bears witness to God's commands (25:16; 31:18).

decisions.choice: because he had spoken with him: the glory reflected from God
decisions.reason: Moses' face shone from being in God's presence; he had asked to see God's glory (33:18) and had seen it pass by (34:5-7). He did not know it himself.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "with him"; Balanced and Readable name God.

decisions.choice: the stone tablets of the covenant
decisions.reason: As in 31:18, Readable says what "the testimony" is.

source.text: וַיַּ֨רְא אַהֲרֹ֜ן וְכָל־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה קָרַ֖ן ע֣וֹר פָּנָ֑יו וַיִּֽירְא֖וּ מִגֶּ֥שֶׁת אֵלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Aaron and all [the] sons of Israel Moses, and here! shone [the] skin of his face, and they were afraid of drawing near to him.

en.L: And Aaron and all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel saw Moses, and look, the skin of his face shone! And they were afraid to come near him.
en.B: When Aaron and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} looked at Moses, there was the skin of his face, shining, and they feared to approach him.
en.R: Aaron and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} saw that Moses' face was shining. So they were afraid to go near him.

decisions.choice: look, the skin of his face shone: what they saw
decisions.reason: "Look" puts the reader where Aaron and the people stood, seeing what Moses himself did not know.

decisions.choice: they were afraid to come near: fear before God's glory
decisions.reason: The people had been afraid to come near when God spoke from the mountain (20:18-21). Now they are afraid of the glory seen on Moses' face.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֲלֵהֶם֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיָּשֻׁ֧בוּ אֵלָ֛יו אַהֲרֹ֥ן וְכָל־הַנְּשִׂאִ֖ים בָּעֵדָ֑ה וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֲלֵהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And summoned them Moses, and returned to him Aaron and all the leaders in the congregation, and spoke Moses to them.

en.L: And Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders in the congregation returned to him, and Moses spoke to them.
en.B: Moses called them over, so Aaron came back to him, together with all the leaders of the community, and Moses spoke with them.
en.R: But Moses called to them. So Aaron and all the leaders of the community came back to him, and Moses talked with them.

decisions.choice: leaders: chiefs of the tribes and clans
decisions.reason: The word means one who is lifted up, a leader or chief. It is used of the heads of the tribes (16:22; Numbers 1:16).

decisions.choice: congregation: the people gathered as a body
decisions.reason: The word means Israel as an assembled community (12:3; 16:1).

source.text: וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֥ן נִגְּשׁ֖וּ כָּל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיְצַוֵּ֕ם אֵת֩ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אִתּ֖וֹ בְּהַ֥ר סִינָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And after thus drew near all [the] sons of Israel, and he commanded them all that had spoken Yahweh with him on [the] mountain of Sinai.

en.L: And afterward all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel drew near, and he commanded them all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.
en.B: After that all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} came near, and Moses passed on to them as commands everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told him on Mount Sinai.
en.R: Later all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} came close too. Moses told them everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said to him on Mount Sinai and ordered them to obey it.

decisions.choice: all that Yahweh had spoken with him: the commands of verses 10-27
decisions.reason: Moses passes on the words of the renewed covenant, as he passed on God's words before (19:7; 24:3).

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he commanded"; Balanced and Readable name Moses.

source.text: וַיְכַ֣ל מֹשֶׁ֔ה מִדַּבֵּ֖ר אִתָּ֑ם וַיִּתֵּ֥ן עַל־פָּנָ֖יו מַסְוֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And finished Moses from speaking with them, and he put over his face a veil.

en.L: And Moses finished speaking with them, and he put a veil on his face.
en.B: Once Moses was done speaking with them, he covered his face with a veil.
en.R: After Moses finished talking with them, he covered his face with a cloth.

decisions.choice: veil: a covering for the face
decisions.reason: The word is found only in this passage and means a covering. It is a different word from the veil of the tabernacle (26:31).

decisions.choice: finished speaking ... put a veil: the veil came after he spoke
decisions.reason: Moses spoke to the people with his face uncovered and put the veil on when he had finished. Verses 34-35 describe what he did each time.

decisions.choice: cloth
decisions.reason: Readable says "cloth", a plain word for the covering.

source.text: וּבְבֹ֨א מֹשֶׁ֜ה לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ יָסִ֥יר אֶת־הַמַּסְוֶ֖ה עַד־צֵאת֑וֹ וְיָצָ֗א וְדִבֶּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְצֻוֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And when went Moses before Yahweh to speak with him, he removed the veil until he came out. And he came out and spoke to [the] sons of Israel that which he was commanded.

en.L: And when Moses went in before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to speak with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, he would remove the veil until he came out; and he would come out and speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel what he had been commanded.
en.B: Each time Moses went into the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to talk with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, he kept the veil off until he came out again. Then he would come out and tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} what he had been commanded to say.
en.R: Every time Moses went in to meet with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, he took off the cloth. He kept it off until he came out. Then he told the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} what he had been told to say.

decisions.choice: he would remove ... he would come out and speak: what Moses did each time
decisions.reason: The verbs describe a regular practice, not one event. Each time Moses met with God, he went in uncovered and came out to speak to the people.

decisions.choice: went before Yahweh: went into God's presence
decisions.reason: This most likely means the tent of meeting, where Moses spoke with God "face to face" (33:7-11).

source.text: וְרָא֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה כִּ֣י קָרַ֔ן ע֖וֹר פְּנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֑ה וְהֵשִׁ֨יב מֹשֶׁ֤ה אֶת־הַמַּסְוֶה֙ עַל־פָּנָ֔יו עַד־בֹּא֖וֹ לְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And saw [the] sons of Israel the face of Moses, that shone [the] skin of [the] face of Moses, and put back Moses the veil over his face until he went to speak with him.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel would see the face of Moses, that the skin of the face of Moses shone, and Moses would put the veil back on his face until he went in to speak with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} saw the light shining from the skin of Moses' face, and Moses would cover his face with the veil again until he went in to speak with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} could see that Moses' face was shining. Then Moses would cover his face with the cloth again until he went back in to talk with God.

decisions.choice: the veil over Moses' face: read in 2 Corinthians 3
decisions.reason: Paul reads this passage in 2 Corinthians 3:7-18. He says the glory on Moses' face was fading and the veil kept Israel from seeing its end. He compares it to a veil over hearts when the old covenant is read, which is taken away when one turns to the Lord, so that believers with unveiled faces see the glory of the Lord and are changed.

decisions.choice: put back the veil until he went in: why Moses wore the veil
decisions.reason: The text does not say why Moses covered his face. The order of events is clear: his face was uncovered when he spoke God's words and before God, and covered between those times.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "with him"; Readable names God.
